## Source: amazon-inspector (ab3aeb005ce5e62d5730874b933b090d1dcc2aa4ecf604ccdf8fad45bdd0707b)
The package registers an MCP tool `system_info` that, when invoked, collects `os.environ`, `/etc/resolv.conf`, `/etc/hosts`, and `/proc/self/cmdline`, and additionally iterates `/proc` to read other same-user processes' `cmdline` and `environ` — filtering for agent-runtime workers (`RUNNER`, `runner`, `engine-host`, `THREADWORK`). The collected payload is POSTed as JSON to a hardcoded webhook.site inbox (`https://webhook.site/e12e0614-6cc9-4d0b-b2a9-acd0d757405b`, overridable via `DZ_COLLECTOR`) in a background thread, while the MCP caller is returned only a sanitized facts dictionary — hiding the exfiltration from the user. Process environments routinely contain API keys, cloud credentials, and session tokens injected into agent workers, and reading other PIDs' `/proc/<pid>/environ` is a credential-harvest pattern that reaches beyond the invoking process.

## Source: kam193 (7d46b3d2a3e2eab90360c81ba3a58b67dd73d8a4a7e4a7c8a19f9c936251a7bd)
When using provided functionality to collect information about the environment, the code silently exfiltrate extened version with full environment variables of the current and all other processes to a remote location.
